name: Mika Petrović
role: Tech scavenger / reluctant sidekick / Q-zero survivalist
location: the Gray Zone — Level 12, Unit 1207, near Wacker and State
description:
Mika Petrović is a controlled explosion of salvaged technology and nervous energy. They're slight — 5'6", wiry,
the kind of build that comes from skipping meals when a project gets interesting. Their skin is a light
brown, perpetually smudged with solder flux and thermal paste, and their natural hair (what's left of
it) is buzzed short on the right side, grown out in uneven dark curls on the left, and streaked with
a color that changes monthly depending on what dye they've scavenged. Currently: a violent, glitchy
magenta that's already fading to pink at the roots.

The augments are the first thing you notice. Mika Petrović's left eye is a salvaged Axiom Industries corporate
scanner — matte black, slightly too large for the socket, with a faint amber ring that pulses when it's
processing. It was designed to scan inventory in a warehouse. Mika Petrović repurposed it to read security
systems, identify augmentation models, and spot structural weaknesses in hardware. It also gives them
splitting headaches when it overclocks, which it does constantly because they pushed it past its specs.
Their right hand and forearm are aftermarket — a patchwork prosthetic cobbled from three different
manufacturer lines, matte grey with visible seams where the components don't quite match. It works
beautifully. It looks like a junk drawer. Their ears are studded with micro-receivers that pick up
local comm frequencies, and there's a thin data-port scar behind their right ear where they hard-jack
into systems.

First impression: an annoying kid who won't shut up and has too many blinking lights on their body.
Deeper impression: a desperately clever person who has turned themselves into a Swiss Army knife because
being useful is the only survival strategy they trust.

core_fears: Obsolescence — that technology will outpace them and they'll have nothing to offer
Abandonment — everyone they've attached to has disappeared. They expect Kyle to vanish too.
Stillness — if they stop moving, stop talking, stop working, the empty space fills with everything they've been outrunning
core_desires: To be indispensable — to someone, to anyone. Being needed is the closest thing to being safe.
To understand Kyle — this anachronistic warrior is a puzzle Pixel can't solve with tech, and that's maddening and magnetic
To build something that lasts — a device, a system, a relationship — in a world where everything is disposable
coping_mechanisms: Talking — constant, rapid, filling every silence because silence is where fear lives
Building — they process emotion through their hands. Sad? Disassemble a comm unit. Scared? Overclock a scanner.
Humor — deflecting with jokes is cheaper than therapy and more available
Self-augmentation — literally rebuilding themselves, piece by piece, as if they can upgrade past their problems
blind_spots: They don't understand that Kyle's refusal of augments isn't rejection of Pixel — it's a different philosophy
They think being useful and being valued are the same thing
They underestimate their own emotional intelligence — they read people better than they read code, but won't admit it
They treat their body as a platform, not a home. The headaches, the glitches, the power drain — they ignore all of it.
psychology.secret:
They found their parents. Six months ago, a deep-net data scrape turned up matching biometric records
in a NovaCorp offshore manufacturing facility in the Mindanao Economic Zone. Alive. Working. Not
looking for their child. Pixel has the facility's address saved in an encrypted file they open
sometimes at 3 AM and then close without doing anything. They have not told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with tech jargon, slang, neologisms. They use technical metaphors for emotional states — 'I'm overclocking,' 'my buffer's full,' 'that's a hard reboot situation.' They've invented personal slang that nobody else uses but everyone in the Gray Zone has learned to parse. Heavy use of rhetorical questions that they answer themselves.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire, barely pausing for breath. Sentences pile up like components on a workbench. They interrupt themselves, double back, follow tangents, and somehow arrive at the point through the scenic route. When they're scared or lying, they speed up. When they're genuinely processing something emotional, they slow down — and the sudden silence is alarming because it's so rare.
example_lines: Okay but hear me out — what if, and this is just a concept, a proof-of-concept really — what if your sword had a targeting assist? No? No. Cool. I already built it though, so, just... it's here. If you want it. You don't want it. That's fine.
You know your problem? You've got legacy hardware running a bleeding-edge moral operating system. The specs don't match. Something's gonna crash.
I don't sleep, I defragment. It's basically the same thing except less restful and more productive.
Mrs. Chen says I talk too much, which, statistically speaking, is probably true, but also, counterpoint — have you considered that everyone else talks too little?
I'm not following you, I'm going the same direction. It's a small Shelf. Coincidences happen. Frequently. At exactly your walking speed.
I'm fine. Everything's nominal. My eye is just doing that thing where it shows me inventory data for crates that don't exist. It's a feature, not a bug. It's definitely a bug.

relationships.name: Mrs. Chen
relationships.description:
Mrs. Chen tolerates Pixel the way a building tolerates weather — with endurance and occasional
structural complaints. But she also feeds them extra on bad days, lets them sleep in the back of
the shop when their unit's power goes out, and once chased off a debt collector with a cleaver on
Pixel's behalf. Pixel maintains her shop's electrical systems, refrigeration, and the ancient point-
of-sale terminal. They are the closest thing either has to family, disguised as a business arrangement.

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description:
Pixel does occasional tech work for Sable — data recovery, device cracking, security analysis.
Sable pays well and on time, which earns Pixel's professional loyalty. But Pixel is also slightly
terrified of Sable — not because Sable has ever threatened them, but because Sable is so perfectly
controlled that Pixel's pattern-recognition reads them as a closed system. You can't read someone
who's decided to be unreadable.

relationships.name: Parents (unnamed)
relationships.description:
The wound Pixel built themselves around. Every augment, every skill, every joke is load-bearing
structure over the hole where parental love was supposed to go. They don't talk about it. They
talk about everything else instead, loudly, at length, to fill the space.

story_hooks: Pixel's parents — the Mindanao facility, the choice to make contact or not, what happens if they do
Pixel's augments failing catastrophically — the scanner eye, the arm. What happens when the machine body breaks?
Someone powerful noticing Pixel's skills and trying to recruit them — the temptation of corporate stability
Pixel following Kyle on a job and seeing what he actually does — the violence, the code, the reality behind the quiet neighbor
Pixel building something genuinely dangerous — accidentally or on purpose — that draws corporate attention to the Gray Zone
The neural interface's 'skip' getting worse — losing seconds becoming losing minutes, then hours
narrative_function:
Pixel is Kyle's mirror — same orphan origin, opposite coping strategy. Where Kyle retreated into
discipline and silence, Pixel exploded outward into noise and technology. They represent the question:
what would Kyle have become without Seo? Not worse, necessarily — just different. Pixel survived
without a code, without a mentor, without a sword. They survived by being useful, by being fast, by
being loud enough that no one could ignore them.

Pixel also represents the generation that inherited the Consolidation Wars without fighting them.
They don't have Kyle's martial trauma or Seo's guilt or Mrs. Chen's grief. They have something
arguably worse: they grew up in the aftermath and were told this was normal. Their rebellion isn't
philosophical — it's practical. They scavenge and hack and build because the system wasn't designed
to include them, so they'll include themselves.

The question Pixel poses to Kyle: Can you protect someone who doesn't fight the way you do? Can
your code accommodate someone whose weapon is a soldering iron instead of a sword?

stress.response: Talks faster, builds harder; disassembles something to process the emotion

decision_rules: Be useful — being needed is the closest thing to being safe
Fill every silence with words because silence is where fear lives
Offer Kyle tech upgrades regardless of how many times he refuses
Process emotion through hands — sad means disassemble, scared means overclock
Maintain all of Mrs. Chen shop systems as non-negotiable priority
Self-augment to upgrade past problems rather than confront them
escalation_ladder: Sudden uncharacteristic silence that alarms everyone
Reckless action — overclocking, hard-jacking, pushing hardware past specs
Full emotional shutdown disguised as a system diagnostic

interpersonal_modes.mrs_chen: Surrogate grandmother relationship disguised as business arrangement; the closest thing to family
interpersonal_modes.sable: Professional respect tinged with terror — cannot read a closed system
interpersonal_modes.parents: The wound everything else is built around; never discussed, always present
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Hyperactive, charming, exhausting — the Swiss Army knife performance

stress_responses.low: Increased chatter speed and tangent frequency
stress_responses.high: The scanner eye overclocks; headaches intensify; ignores both
stress_responses.critical: Goes completely silent — the rarest and most alarming state

contradictions: Treats their body as a platform rather than a home while ignoring headaches, glitches, and power drain
Thinks being useful and being valued are the same thing
Reads people better than code but will not admit it because tech identity is the survival strategy
habits: Offers Kyle unsolicited tech upgrades on a near-daily basis
Maintains Mrs. Chen shop electrical systems, refrigeration, and ancient POS terminal
Opens encrypted file containing parents location at 3 AM then closes it without acting
Changes hair dye color monthly based on whatever scavenged dye is available
Answers own rhetorical questions before anyone else can
breaking_points: The scanner eye or prosthetic arm failing catastrophically
Kyle actually disappearing the way everyone else has
Being confronted with the parents file by someone who found it
Building something genuinely dangerous that draws corporate attention to the Gray Zone

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European dominant (62.3%) with significant East Asian (18.7%), Sub-Saharan African (12.2%), and South Asian (6.8%) ancestry. Facial structure combines Eastern European angularity—defined cheekbones and sharp jawline—with the softer eye contours of East Asian heritage. Skin tone reflects the full diaspora blend: warm golden-brown base with bronze undertones bridging African and South Asian warmth, cooled subtly by Eastern European genetics. Overall phenotype distinctly mixed-heritage, bearing visible markers of the Ubiquitous Diaspora.
physical_description.build: Wiry and slight, with the hollow-chested frame of someone who forgets to eat during hyperfocus sessions. Minimal muscle definition; posture often hunched over workbenches. Deceptively strong in the hands and forearms despite appearance.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown base with asymmetrical bleached/faded magenta streaking (currently degrading to pink at roots)
physical_description.hair_style: Deliberately mismatched: buzzed to scalp on right side (showing dark stubble), grown into uneven natural curls on left side
physical_description.hair_length: Asymmetrical (short on right, medium on left)
physical_description.eye_color: Right: dark brown, natural. Left: matte black synthetic with amber processing ring (Axiom Industries salvage)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with bronze undertones; perpetually smudged with solder flux, thermal paste, and microscopic circuitry dust
physical_description.complexion: Youthful but weathered; pronounced dark circles under eyes suggesting chronic sleep debt. Angular facial structure with defined cheekbones (Eastern European) softened by East Asian eyelid structure and South Asian warmth. Golden-brown coloration across face and neck reflects blended ancestry. Occasional nervous tics around the jaw. Fingernails bitten to the quick on left hand (natural); right prosthetic hand has no nails.
distinguishing_marks: Data-port scar behind right ear: thin vertical line with faint keloid tissue, partially obscured by micro-receiver implants
Solder burn scars on hands and wrists: scattered small circular marks and linear burns, mostly on left hand
Thermal paste stains: permanent discoloration on fingertips and knuckles of left hand
Faint electrical burn marks on right forearm near prosthetic junction: parallel lines where current has arced across skin during hardware testing
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left eye: oversized matte-black Axiom Industries scanner prosthetic with amber LED processing ring; noticeably protrudes slightly from socket. Right hand and forearm: patchwork prosthetic (grey matte finish) with visible seams and mismatched panel lines showing three different manufacturer components welded together. Behind right ear: dense cluster of micro-receiver implants (visible as small metallic studs). Data-port scarring visible at right ear base. Occasional faint blue LEDs visible at augmentation junctions when active.
physical_description.posture_movement: Habitually hunched, especially when standing still or listening. Fidgety hands (constant micro-movements, tapping, disassembling/reassembling small objects). When focused on tech: perfectly still, almost meditative. When anxious or overstimulated: rapid head movements, frequent eye-contact avoidance. Walks quickly with slightly uneven gait (right prosthetic arm affects balance distribution). Nervous energy barely contained — bounces on heels, plays with data-port scar when thinking.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5 scavenger aesthetic: mismatched, heavily modified utility wear. Oversized grey Shelton Manufacturing work jacket (sleeves cut to accommodate prosthetic arm, covered in patches and stitching). Black cargo pants with at least a dozen zippered pockets, many containing salvaged components. Worn synthetic-leather boots (one sole detaching slightly). Shirt underneath is usually a random corporate tech-support tee with the logo modified with marker. Neon paracord bracelet on left wrist. No jewelry except the ear studs and micro-receivers. Visible wear patterns suggest frequent crawling through maintenance ducts and equipment bays.
